Can you explain quantum computing?
Just now
Quantum computing uses quantum bits (qubits) that can exist in multiple states simultaneously thanks to superposition. Unlike classical bits that are either 0 or 1, qubits can be both at once, enabling parallel computation.
Just now
That's fascinating! Can you give me a simple example?
Just now
Sure! Imagine searching through a phone book with 1 million names. A classical computer checks one by one. A quantum computer using Grover's algorithm could find the right name in roughly 1,000 steps instead of 500,000 — a quadratic speedup!
